html:
A movement for social equality launched in 1925 in the Tamil country of south India, led by E. V. Ramasamy, known as Periyar. It attacked the caste system and the dominance of Brahmins in religion, education and government jobs.

Periyar had left the Congress after the Vaikom Satyagraha, judging it too soft on caste. The movement urged lower castes to claim self-respect rather than wait for reform from above. It promoted rationalism and atheism, women's rights and widow remarriage. It popularised "self-respect marriages", held without Brahmin priests or Sanskrit rites, which Tamil Nadu later made legal.

It merged with the non-Brahmin Justice Party and in 1944 became the Dravidar Kazhagam. In 1949 Periyar's follower C. N. Annadurai broke away to found the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, which entered elections and won power in Tamil Nadu in 1967. Since then Dravidian parties have ruled the state, and Tamil Nadu's wide caste quotas in jobs and colleges trace back to this movement. It sits beside Ambedkar's campaigns, such as the Mahad Satyagraha, as a main strand of the fight against caste.
